measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Town Council terms from two years to four years beginning with the November 7, 2028 election. In that election, the four highest-vote candidates would receive four-year terms and the other three would receive two-year terms; later terms would be four years, with no more than four seats up in one election. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the four-year terms and the stated 2028 transition to staggered elections.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to council terms and elections.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Change the treasurer from elected to appointed by the town administrator with at least four council votes and an initial contract of no more than three years. Require a bachelor’s degree and five years of accounting or equivalent financial experience, plus any council-set qualifications. The treasurer would report to the administrator and report to the council on municipal finances when requested. Expand financial advice to all municipal collective-bargaining agreements and remove the exception for those agreements and Budget Committee requests from advice on transactions above $500,000. The treasurer elected in November 2024 would finish that term unless the office becomes vacant through resignation, illness or death, when the new appointment process could be used. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the appointed treasurer, qualifications, duties and protection of the current elected term.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject these proposed changes to the town treasurer position.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Change the clerk from elected to appointed by the town administrator with at least four council votes and an initial contract of no more than three years. Allow additional duties assigned by the administrator and remove the outdated Financial Town Referendum duties. The clerk elected and qualified in November 2026 would finish that elected term. A vacancy during that term through resignation, illness or death would be filled by the council for the rest of the term; the new appointment process would apply afterward. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the appointed clerk and duties, preserving the November 2026 elected term as specified.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed appointment system for the town clerk.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Require a town planner appointed by the administrator with council approval. Initial and renewal contracts could each last no more than three years, and the council would set qualifications. The planner would advise the Planning Board on land use, development rules, economic growth, long-term planning, sustainability and environmental protection, including reviewing proposals and making recommendations. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the required planner position, contract limits and planning duties.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed charter requirement for a town planner.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Let the council acquire, sell, transfer or lease real property, subject to voter approval for transfers of town land or property rights held for open space, recreation or conservation. For those voter-approved transactions, publish all material terms on the town website and by any other council-chosen method at least 21 days before a regular or special election. Preserve exceptions for transfers restricting land use for conservation or preservation, or connected to public utilities or similar services. Remove the former five-year expiration of voter approval and the exemption for leases of ten years or less. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve those property powers, voter-approval protections, notice requirement and exceptions.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed change to town land-transaction rules.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Remove the Budget Committee as an elected town body by deleting its charter article and the provision requiring it to prepare and submit a proposed unified budget and implementation language to the council. Those charter sections would be reserved or renumbered. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve removing the Budget Committee and its charter budget duties.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed removal of the committee’s charter provisions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Reduce the Harbor and Coastal Waters Management Commission from nine members to seven and remove the Planning Board membership requirement. Keep council-appointed two-year terms, staggered so no more than four expire in one year, and preference for representation of boating, fishing, waterfront-property and conservation interests. A vacancy would be filled from the same interest group for the remaining term. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the seven-member commission, revised staggering and removal of the Planning Board seat requirement.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Reduce the Planning Board from nine members to seven and specify that it works with and receives advice from the town planner on land use and development. Keep council appointments of town voters to staggered three-year terms, with no more than one-third expiring in a year, and the bar on town elected officials and employees serving. Require the board to elect a chair, vice-chair, secretary and any other officers annually from its members. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the seven-member Planning Board, planner-advice provision and officer-election rules.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed set of Planning Board changes.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Clarify that the Personnel Board interviews selected applicants for full-time and part-time jobs and checks their application information and references. For town administrator, the council would approve the job description before advertising; the Personnel Board would review applications, interview those it finds qualified and recommend applicants to the council. The council would remain responsible for hiring the administrator. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the clarified council and Personnel Board roles in reviewing and interviewing applicants.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Update the Zoning Board’s powers by reference to state zoning law and specify that it hears appeals from the administrative officer. Keep five regular members and two alternates appointed by the council from town voters, with five-year regular terms and one-year alternate terms. Alternates could participate in matters but vote only when replacing an absent regular member and after attending all hearings on that matter. Bar both regular and alternate members from being town elected officials or employees; the first alternate would fill a regular vacancy, with a new alternate appointed. Require annual chair and vice-chair selection and allow council removal for cause after a public hearing. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the revised zoning-appeal, alternate-member, officer-selection and removal provisions.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Revise the Economic Development Commission’s duties to work with current state agencies; recruit businesses consistent with the town’s comprehensive plan, character and tax-base diversification goals; share state-program information; develop business networking; create a public database of vacant commercial and industrial properties; and work with the town planner on commercial storefront and streetscape improvements. Continue assistance to town businesses, particularly marine and agricultural businesses, on tax relief, low-cost loans and grants for startup, expansion or renovation. Remove the obsolete Enterprise Zone assistance reference. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve those revised economic-development duties and removal of the obsolete reference.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed Economic Development Commission update.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Require the School Committee to choose officers, including chair and vice-chair, from its elected members, with those officers serving as long as a majority of the committee supports them. Remove the annual officer-election requirement. Effect would also require General Assembly ratification if necessary.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve officers chosen from the committee’s elected members and serving at its pleasure, without the annual-election requirement.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed School Committee clarification.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize the Town Council to sell the unimproved town parcel at 0 Poplar Street, Map 201 Lot 125, at fair market value as determined by the tax assessor. The ballot identifies the parcel as having no municipal use or benefit.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve selling that parcel at the tax assessor’s determination of fair market value.
measureRecords.noMeans: Reject this proposed authority to sell that parcel.
